ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, an amide/carbonyl-related transition-state structure can be seen: the left side is labeled Me2N, connected to the central carbonyl carbon; a double bond is drawn between the central carbon and the O above; the right side of the central carbon is connected to H. The figure also has curved arrows and a R−M/negative-sign label below. Reasoning: According to the meaning of the question, ignore the arrows, and exclude all bonds involving hydrogen. In Me2N, two N–Me single bonds are implicit, count 2; the single bond between N and the carbonyl carbon counts 1; the carbonyl C=O double bond counts according to bond order as 2; the C–H bond involves hydrogen and is not counted. Therefore the total is 2 + 1 + 2 = 5.
